intent: Rare Candy is the only way to reach Dragapult ex on the turn Dreepy lands and the agent scores that line 40000; one Lucky Helmet is a singleton tool it scores 15.
Boss's Orders is what converts the Phantom Dive plan into the target it selected; Brock Scouting is a second setup Supporter competing for the same one-per-turn slot.
Team Rocket's Watchtower is scored 4000 only when another stadium is out; a fourth Poke Pad always finds the Dreepy or Drakloak the line needs.
Budew's item lock is the deck's tempo defence and the agent plays it at 30000 from turn two; Meowth ex is a one-of that only matters when no Supporter has been played.
Night Stretcher recovers the exact Pokemon or energy the hand score is missing; the singleton tool does not.
Phantom Dive costs two energy and the agent attaches one per turn; the fourth Crushing Hammer is a disruption card in a deck that wins by attacking.
Unfair Stamp scores 80000 only after a knockout; a third Rare Candy raises the probability of the turn-two Dragapult ex the whole deck is built around.
A fourth Dragapult ex is a fourth copy of the only attacker; Latias ex only matters when the active is one of three specific non-attackers.
The deck attacks with Psychic and carries Fire only for Crispin; if the fourth Fire is dead, more search finds the line.
Drop the second setup Supporter entirely and spend both slots on cards that work on any turn, not only before a Supporter has been used.
Trade disruption for reach: Boss's Orders is scored 60000 whenever the plan names a benched target, which is the deck's three-prize turn.
Buddy-Buddy Poffin puts the basics down for free; Ultra Ball costs two cards from a hand the agent already scores as negative when it discards.
Combination arm: the two single changes most likely to be individually positive, to test whether they compose or compete.
Combination arm on the consistency axis alone: more Rare Candy and more Poke Pad, paid for by two situational one-ofs.
